I believe you are referring to the renowned Hittitologist Ludwig Güterbock. He was a German-born American scholar who made significant contributions to the study of the ancient Hittite civilization.

Güterbock was born in Berlin, Germany on September 22, 1917, and later moved to the United States where he became a naturalized citizen. He studied at the University of Berlin and received his Ph.D. in Near Eastern Studies from the University of Chicago in 1950.

He taught at the University of Chicago, the Oriental Institute, and the University of Pennsylvania. Güterbock was known for his expertise in Hittite language and culture, and he published numerous articles and books on the subject.

He was a key figure in deciphering the Hittite language and his work helped to shed light on the history and culture of the Hittite Empire. He also conducted archaeological excavations in Turkey, where the Hittites once thrived.

Ludwig Güterbock passed away on March 29, 2000, leaving behind a legacy of scholarship and research that has greatly advanced our understanding of the ancient Hittite civilization.
